policy:
# METADATA
# title: S3 Gateway (s0) data-plane authorization
# description: |
#   The policy the S3 gateway evaluates for every parsed S3 request (and for every
#   sub-decision the gateway decomposes a request into: one multi-delete key, the
#   source-read / dest-write halves of a copy, …).
#
#   The engine reads ONE rule: `data.s3.authz.decision`, which returns
#
#     { "allow": bool, "reason": string, "obligations": object }
#
#   — not a bare boolean like `ceph.authz`. `reason` is audit-facing: a deny
#   reason matters as much as an allow reason in a regulated trail, and it names
#   the deciding layer so a 403 is diagnosable. `obligations` are side-effects the
#   PEP MUST apply to a permitted request before forwarding (see below); they only
#   exist because the gateway is on the parsed path.
#
#   ## input (OpaInput v2 — see s0 `src/authz/input.rs`)
#
#     input.principal.{sub, type, attributes}   type ∈ {"user","service_account"}
#     input.tenant            harbor slug == Ceph tenant
#     input.organization_id   the org this bundle must belong to
#     input.action            one of the 6 settled verbs (below)
#     input.bucket            "" for account-scoped ops (ListBuckets)
#     input.object?           object key, present for object-shaped ops
#     input.prefix?           list prefix, present for ListObjects*
#     input.request.attributes  { "<key>": ["<value>", …] }  request-context ABAC
#
#   Deliberately NOT read here: `input.operation` (the exact s3s op name). The verb
#   is what authorizes; the operation name exists for the audit record. Reading it
#   would put 99 op names into the authorization surface and into the decision
#   cache key for no gain.
#
#   ## data (the `/s3-gateway-bundle` document — see
#   ##  `handlers/vauban/s3_gateway_projection/bundle.rs`)
#
#     data.grant_schema_version : 2                      ← §1.6 gate, hard deny on mismatch
#     data.org_settings.{freeze_writes, organization_id, bundle_revision}
#     data.tenants[t].user_attributes[<subject_key>].{groups, attributes}
#     data.tenants[t].bucket_attributes[b].{denylist{<RAW sub>: true}, freeze_writes, sensitivity?}
#     data.tenants[t].s3_grants[<subject_key>]  : [Grant]
#     data.tenants[t].s3_deny[<subject_key>]    : [Grant]   ← v2 only; ABSENT ⇒ hard deny
#     data.tenants[t].group_grants              : {} (contractually empty)
#
#     Grant := { "bucket": "<name>"|"*",
#                "actions":   ["read_objects", …],   # explicit verbs, never "*"
#                "prefixes":  ["team-a/"],           # [] ⇒ THE WHOLE BUCKET
#                "conditions":[ {"kind","key","value"} ] }   # [] ⇒ unconditional
#
#   ## Two key spaces, on purpose (§1.7)
#
#   Grants, membership and group lookup are keyed by `subject_key` — `user:<oidc
#   sub>` / `sa:<client id>` — derived HERE by sprintf, mirroring `console.rego`.
#   The per-bucket DENYLIST is keyed by the **raw** `input.principal.sub`, because
#   it is projected from `HFBucket.spec.denylist`, an untyped `Vec<String>` on the
#   CRD with no user/service-account discriminator. Re-keying it would need a CRD
#   schema change, a writer and a migration. Both key spaces are pinned by test,
#   in both directions: `test_the_denylist_is_keyed_on_the_raw_sub`,
#   `test_the_denylist_is_not_keyed_on_the_subject_key`,
#   `test_grants_are_keyed_on_the_subject_key_not_the_raw_sub`.
#
#   `subject_key` has NO `default`: an unrecognized `principal.type` leaves it
#   undefined, `subject_key_present` is false, and the decision falls to deny.
#
#   ## Fail-closed discipline (the rules this module is written under)
#
#   1. `default allow := false`, and every complete rule whose body can be
#      undefined carries an explicit `default`. UNDEFINED IS NOT FALSE: a rule
#      reference that evaluates to undefined makes the enclosing body undefined,
#      and a `decision` assembled from undefined parts is itself undefined — the
#      PEP then receives no decision at all. Measured with `opa eval` (1.13.1):
#      `not m[input.x]` is `true` when `x` is present and the key is missing, but
#      UNDEFINED when `input.x` itself is absent. Presence is therefore always
#      tested by shape (`is_string`/`is_object`/`is_array`) or by an explicit
#      `default`, never by negation. Partial-set rules and comprehension rules are
#      total by construction (they yield the empty set/array) and need none.
#   2. Never test a condition by absence (`not g.condition`): that is TRUE when
#      the field is boolean `false`, i.e. an unconditional allow (accepted defect
#      C-3). Conditions are tested by SHAPE — `is_array(g.conditions)` — so a
#      grant whose `conditions` is missing or malformed applies to nothing.
#   3. Every bucket-scoped rule is gated on `bucket_scoped`, or a
#      `"bucket": "*"` grant silently matches the empty string and authorizes
#      account-scoped ops (accepted defect B-2). `bucket_scoped` is a SHAPE test
#      (`is_string` AND non-empty), not the value test `input.bucket != ""` that
#      guarded these sites before review finding F3: `null != ""`, `0 != ""` and
#      `{} != ""` are all TRUE in Rego, so a non-string bucket passed every B-2
#      gate while `bucket_attributes[input.bucket]` went undefined — silently
#      disarming the per-bucket freeze and the per-bucket denylist at once.
#   4. `prefixes: []` means THE WHOLE BUCKET. `visible_buckets: []` means NOTHING
#      VISIBLE. Opposite empty-case semantics; both are pinned by test.
#   5. Deny overrides allow, unconditionally and regardless of specificity.
#
#   ## Obligations emitted
#
#     {"excluded_prefixes": [...], "must_understand": ["excluded_prefixes"]}
#         ListObjects*: deny-grant prefixes that fall INSIDE the listing scope.
#         The PEP must filter those keys out of the response.
#     {"all_buckets_visible": true}                       ListBuckets, unrestricted
#     {"visible_buckets": [...], "must_understand": ["visible_buckets"]}
#         ListBuckets: the exact bucket set the response may contain.
#
#   ## ListBuckets visibility keys on `read`, and is INCLUSIVE of prefix scopes
#
#   Since 2026-08-08 the verb behind ListBuckets is `read` — the projection of the
#   catalog's dual-plane `bucket:read`, which is also what the console's bucket
#   list/detail routes check. That is the point: one grant, one answer, whichever
#   PEP is asked.
#
#   A bucket is visible when the principal holds ANY applicable `read` grant that
#   names it — whole-bucket OR prefix-scoped — or a `"*"` grant, which is
#   enumerated against `bucket_attributes` so the deny subtraction can apply.
#   Prefix-scoped counts because ListBuckets discloses only the NAME, and a
#   principal scoped to `warehouse/team-a/*` already has to know `warehouse` to
#   use its own grant at all. Hiding it would buy no secrecy and would make
#   `aws s3 ls` empty for a principal whose next command works.
#
#   `read` in `bucket_actions` (HeadBucket, GetBucketLocation) is satisfied by the
#   same grants for the same reason, and NOT gated on `whole_bucket`. The
#   whole-bucket rule exists so a prefix-scoped grant cannot confer a bucket-level
#   POWER — it was written for `delete_bucket` / `write_bucket_config` /
#   `manage_lifecycle`, none of which exist here any more. Applying it to `read`
#   would make ListBuckets and HeadBucket disagree about whether the same bucket
#   exists for the same principal, which is precisely the two-answers-to-one-
#   question defect the vocabulary change was made to remove — and it is what
#   breaks every client that probes with HeadBucket before writing.
#
#   `must_understand` names obligations the PEP must implement or DENY (accepted
#   defect C-5): an obligation a PEP silently drops is a fail-open.
package s3.authz

import rego.v1

# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The settled vocabulary — 6 verbs (was 13, cut 2026-08-08)
#
# THE GATEWAY IS DATA-PLANE ONLY. Objects, and the listing of objects. Everything
# about the bucket as a MANAGED resource — whether it exists at all, its policy,
# its CORS, its quota — is decided by the console and the operator, which is what
# creates and maintains the `HFBucket` CR. A bucket made over S3 has no CR: it is
# unmanaged, unquota'd, invisible to the console, and absent from the
# `bucket_attributes` map THIS MODULE reads its own freeze switch and denylist
# from. So `create_bucket`, `delete_bucket`, `read_bucket_config` and
# `write_bucket_config` are not merely removed verbs — they were the ways to
# create state this policy cannot see.
#
# `read_bucket` + `list_buckets` were not dropped but MERGED UPWARD into `read`,
# the catalog's dual-plane `bucket:read`; `read_object_tags` merged into
# `read_objects`; `write_object_acl` went with the rest of bucket/object posture.
#
# Grouped by REQUEST SHAPE, because the shape decides which scope test applies.
# `bucket:manage_lifecycle` is deliberately absent: its rego branch was the only
# keyless bucket branch and granted the whole bucket ignoring prefixes.
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Need a key. A grant's `prefixes` scope them.
#
# `read_objects` also authorizes `GetObjectTagging`: reading an object's tags is
# strictly less than reading the object itself, so a separate verb bought
# nothing. `write_object_tags` is NOT merged the same way — see `write_actions`.
object_actions := {
	"read_objects",
	"write_objects",
	"delete_objects",
	"write_object_tags",
}

# Enumerates keys. Scoped by `prefixes` AND narrowed by deny grants.
list_actions := {"list_objects"}

# Act on the bucket itself — `HeadBucket`, `GetBucketLocation`. Exactly one verb,
# and it is purely informational: it discloses that the bucket exists, never a
# key, never a byte, and it mutates nothing.
#
# NOTE: this set and `account_actions` deliberately SHARE the verb `read`, because
# one permission answers one question ("does this bucket exist, for me?") in two
# request shapes. They are kept apart by the `bucket_scoped` / `account_scoped`
# shape gates, which partition `input.bucket` and are mutually exclusive — every
# rule that reads either set carries the matching gate. Adding a verb to only one
# of these sets is fine; adding one to both without its shape gate is not.
bucket_actions := {"read"}

# Account-scoped: `input.bucket` is "". `ListBuckets`.
account_actions := {"read"}

# HISTORY, kept because the reasoning outlives the verbs. `prefix_defeating_
# bucket_actions` used to be `{"delete_bucket", "write_bucket_config"}`: the two
# bucket verbs that could DEFEAT or DESTROY what a prefix-scoped deny protects
# (review finding F4) — one destroys the denied keys, the other rewrites the
# bucket policy that keeps them unreachable — so ANY applicable deny in the bucket
# blocked them, whatever verb the deny named. Both verbs are gone: bucket
# lifecycle and bucket posture are control-plane now, and the only bucket-shaped
# verb left, `read`, can neither destroy nor unprotect anything. The set and its
# `explicit_deny` clause are therefore removed rather than left empty — dead rego
# that can never fire is how a future reader mistakes a removed rule for a live
# one. If a bucket-mutating verb is ever added back, that clause comes back with
# it.

all_actions := ((object_actions | list_actions) | bucket_actions) | account_actions

# The 3 verbs the `freeze_writes` kill switch stops. Pinned by
# `test_the_write_set_is_exactly_the_settled_three` here; §1.2 requires it to be
# cross-asserted against s0's `Action::is_write()` as well, which is owed by
# s0 stage 3: a divergence is a `freeze_writes` bypass.
#
# `write_object_tags` stays a separate verb from `write_objects` ON PURPOSE and
# must not be merged into it. `OpaInput.object_tags` exists so a policy can key on
# an object's tags; the moment one does, a principal holding both could re-tag its
# way into whatever that policy keys on — it would grant itself the condition.
# Merging them plants a trap that springs the day tag-driven ABAC is switched on.
write_actions := {
	"write_objects",
	"delete_objects",
	"write_object_tags",
}

# The bundle shape this module was written for. A mismatch is a HARD deny (§1.6):
# the previously shipped module had no deny rule at all, so a projected deny grant
# evaluated as an ALLOW. Gating on the version makes old-module + new-bundle
# deny-all instead of allow-all.
expected_grant_schema_version := 2

# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The single rule the engine reads
#
# Strict precedence, mutually exclusive via `else`, terminal clause denies. The
# guards are ALSO repeated inside `allow` (defense in depth): the else-chain
# decides the reason, `allow` decides authorization, and
# `test_decision_allow_never_disagrees_with_the_allow_rule` pins them together.
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

decision := deny_with("deny: bundle grant_schema_version is not the expected version") if not schema_ok

else := deny_with("deny: bundle organization does not match the request") if not org_matches

else := deny_with("deny: unrecognized principal type") if not subject_key_present

else := deny_with("deny: tenant is not present in this bundle") if not tenant_known

else := deny_with("deny: bundle carries no deny dimension") if deny_dimension_missing

else := deny_with("deny: org or bucket writes frozen (freeze_writes)") if frozen

else := deny_with("deny: principal on bucket denylist") if denylisted

else := deny_with("deny: principal is not a tenant member") if not member

else := deny_with("deny: explicit deny grant") if explicit_deny

else := deny_with("deny: listing scope falls inside a deny grant") if list_leak_deny

else := {"allow": true, "reason": "allow: grant matched", "obligations": obligations} if allow

else := deny_with("deny: no grant matches action and scope")

# A denial carries no obligations: an obligation is something the PEP applies to a
# request it is about to forward.
deny_with(r) := {"allow": false, "reason": r, "obligations": {}}

# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Authorization
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

default allow := false

allow if {
	schema_ok
	org_matches
	subject_key_present
	tenant_known
	not deny_dimension_missing
	not frozen
	not denylisted
	member
	not explicit_deny
	not list_leak_deny
	grant_matches
}

# ── bundle integrity gates ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

default schema_ok := false

schema_ok if data.grant_schema_version == expected_grant_schema_version

# The bundle is published per organization. If s0 ever pairs an org's request with
# another org's bundle, every grant lookup would still "work" — against foreign
# data. Fail closed: an absent or non-string `organization_id` denies.
default org_matches := false

org_matches if {
	is_string(data.org_settings.organization_id)
	data.org_settings.organization_id == input.organization_id
}

default tenant_known := false

tenant_known if is_object(data.tenants[input.tenant])

# At schema version 2 the deny dimension is ALWAYS emitted, `{}` included. A
# MISSING `s3_deny` therefore is not "no denies exist" — it is a v1 document
# wearing a v2 version number, or a truncated one. Hard deny; combined with the
# version gate it should be unreachable.
#
# The gate covers the per-subject entry too, and that half is the one that
# matters. `deny_grants` iterates `s3_deny[subject_key]`; if that entry is
# present but is not an array, the iteration yields nothing and the principal
# reads as "has no denies" — a REVOCATION SILENTLY INVERTED TO AN ALLOW, which
# is exactly the D-1 failure this module exists to prevent, one level further
# down the document. The allow side needs no equivalent gate: a malformed
# `s3_grants[subject_key]` yields no grants, which denies.
#
# Measured on the corrupted document under regorus: without the second clause a
# `read_objects` request whose deny entry had been replaced by `""` returned
# `allow: grant matched`. With it, `deny: bundle carries no deny dimension`.
default deny_dimension_missing := true

deny_dimension_missing := false if {
	is_object(data.tenants[input.tenant].s3_deny)
	subject_deny_entry_well_formed
}

# Vacuously true when the principal has no entry at all — the ordinary case for
# a principal nobody has denied anything.
default subject_deny_entry_well_formed := true

subject_deny_entry_well_formed := false if {
	entry := data.tenants[input.tenant].s3_deny[subject_key]
	not is_array(entry)
}

# ── identity ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Kind-namespaced subject key, built here so a service account whose client id
# collides with a user's OIDC subject can never resolve that user's grants. Same
# convention as `console.rego:66-68` — the two PEPs read one projection.
#
# NO `default` ON PURPOSE: an unrecognized `principal.type` leaves this undefined,
# so `subject_key_present` is false and the decision falls to deny.
#
# `is_string(input.principal.sub)` is the F3 shape rule applied to the OTHER key
# space. Without it a non-string sub still produced a STRING key — sprintf's `%s`
# renders a number as `user:%!s(int=5)` and an object as `user:{"a": 1}` (both
# measured under opa 1.13.1) — so `subject_key_present` held and the request was
# denied only by luck, when no bundle key happened to collide. Worse, the
# denylist compares the RAW sub with `==` against its string keys (§1.7), so a
# non-string sub is unreachable by the denylist while `subject_key` still looks
# well-formed: the two key spaces would disagree about the same principal.
# Making the shape explicit turns that into "deny: unrecognized principal type".
subject_key := sprintf("user:%s", [input.principal.sub]) if {
	input.principal.type == "user"
	is_string(input.principal.sub)
}

subject_key := sprintf("sa:%s", [input.principal.sub]) if {
	input.principal.type == "service_account"
	is_string(input.principal.sub)
}

default subject_key_present := false

subject_key_present if is_string(subject_key)

default member := false

member if is_object(data.tenants[input.tenant].user_attributes[subject_key])

# The ABAC source is the BUNDLE, never the caller's token: token claims are frozen
# at mint, so sourcing attributes from them would make an attribute (or role)
# change non-revocable until the session expires. Multi-valued — matching is
# membership, exactly as `console.rego:103-106`.
default principal_attributes := {}

principal_attributes := attrs if {
	attrs := data.tenants[input.tenant].user_attributes[subject_key].attributes
	is_object(attrs)
}

default principal_groups := []

principal_groups := groups if {
	groups := data.tenants[input.tenant].user_attributes[subject_key].groups
	is_array(groups)
}

default request_attributes := {}

request_attributes := attrs if {
	attrs := input.request.attributes
	is_object(attrs)
}

# ── request shape (review finding F3) ───────────────────────────────────────
#
# `input.bucket` decides which scope test applies, so EVERY rule that branches on
# it goes through one of these two shape gates. They are mutually exclusive and
# jointly partial: a bucket that is not a string satisfies NEITHER, so such a
# request is bucket-scoped nowhere and account-scoped nowhere, and falls to the
# terminal deny.
#
# The predecessor guarded these sites with the VALUE test `input.bucket != ""`.
# Measured with opa 1.13.1 against a subject holding
# `{"bucket":"*","prefixes":[]}`, before the fix:
#
#   {"action":"write_objects","bucket":null,"object":"x"}    -> allow: grant matched
#   {"action":"write_objects","bucket":0,   "object":"x"}    -> allow: grant matched
#   {"action":"write_objects","bucket":{"x":1},"object":"x"} -> allow: grant matched
#
# …while the same request naming a genuinely frozen bucket denied. `null != ""`
# is TRUE, so `bucket_matches` fired on the `"*"` branch, and both
# `bucket_freeze_engaged` and `denylisted` vanished because
# `bucket_attributes[null]` is undefined. Only the ORG-wide freeze still caught
# it. Not reachable from today's s0 (`OpaInput.bucket: String`) — but `bucket` is
# being reshaped by tasks 24/61, and this is module rule 1 at the exact gate §2.1
# singles out as B-2.

default bucket_scoped := false

bucket_scoped if {
	is_string(input.bucket)
	input.bucket != ""
}

# `is_string` here is belt-and-braces and is KNOWN not to change any outcome:
# `null == ""` is already false, so equality alone fails closed. It is kept so
# the two gates read as one partition of the same field rather than as two
# unrelated tests — the next person to add a bucket branch copies one of these,
# and both must carry the shape. Removing it passes the suite; that is expected,
# not evidence that it is dead.
default account_scoped := false

account_scoped if {
	is_string(input.bucket)
	input.bucket == ""
}

# ── the org-wide / per-bucket write kill switch ─────────────────────────────

default frozen := false

frozen if {
	is_write_action
	write_freeze_engaged
}

# FAIL SAFE: the default is FROZEN. Only an org_settings document that explicitly
# says `freeze_writes == false` thaws writes — a missing document, a missing
# field, or a malformed value ("false", 0, null) leaves the freeze engaged. The
# kill switch must survive a broken bundle, which is precisely when it is used.
default write_freeze_engaged := true

write_freeze_engaged := false if {
	data.org_settings.freeze_writes == false
	not bucket_freeze_engaged
}

# `HFBucket.spec.freeze_writes` — the per-bucket half. Absence means "this bucket
# is not individually frozen", NOT "frozen": a bucket with no HFBucket CR has no
# attributes at all, and the org-wide switch above is the fail-safe that covers a
# broken/absent bundle. A write to such a bucket still needs an explicit grant.
default bucket_freeze_engaged := false

bucket_freeze_engaged if {
	bucket_scoped
	data.tenants[input.tenant].bucket_attributes[input.bucket].freeze_writes == true
}

default is_write_action := false

is_write_action if input.action in write_actions

# An action outside the settled vocabulary is treated as MUTATING for the
# purposes of the kill switch (defense in depth — such an action also matches no
# grant rule and is denied anyway).
is_write_action if not input.action in all_actions

# ── the per-bucket denylist (RAW sub — a different key space, §1.7) ──────────
#
# Keyed on `input.principal.sub`, NOT on `subject_key`. Membership is by KEY
# PRESENCE, not by the value being truthy: a malformed `{"<sub>": false}` must not
# be able to un-deny a principal the operator listed.

default denylisted := false

denylisted if {
	bucket_scoped
	denylist := data.tenants[input.tenant].bucket_attributes[input.bucket].denylist
	is_object(denylist)
	some denied_sub, _ in denylist
	denied_sub == input.principal.sub
}

# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Effective grants
#
# Partial set rules: total by construction (the empty set when nothing matches),
# so they need no `default`.
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

grants contains g if {
	subject_grants := data.tenants[input.tenant].s3_grants[subject_key]
	is_array(subject_grants)
	some g in subject_grants
}

# `group_grants` is contractually `{}` — the SQL resolver already expands every
# group binding onto each member's own subject, so this branch yields nothing
# today. It exists, keyed on `subject_key`, because §1.7 counts group membership
# as one of the four sites that had to move off the raw sub: if the map is ever
# populated, it must resolve through the same key space as everything else rather
# than silently dropping every group-derived grant.
#
# Groups are read LIVE from the bundle (`user_attributes[subject_key].groups`) and
# never from the caller's token, so a group removal revokes immediately instead of
# at token expiry. Deny-overrides still applies to a group-derived allow — the
# deny layer is evaluated independently of where an allow came from.
grants contains g if {
	some group in principal_groups
	bound := data.tenants[input.tenant].group_grants[group]
	is_array(bound)
	some g in bound
}

deny_grants contains g if {
	subject_denies := data.tenants[input.tenant].s3_deny[subject_key]
	is_array(subject_denies)
	some g in subject_denies
}

# ── grant matching primitives ───────────────────────────────────────────────

# B-2: gated on a non-empty bucket, or `"bucket": "*"` matches the empty string
# and an org-wide grant silently authorizes account-scoped ops like ListBuckets.
bucket_matches(g) if {
	bucket_scoped
	g.bucket == input.bucket
}

bucket_matches(g) if {
	bucket_scoped
	g.bucket == "*"
}

# NO `"*" in g.actions` wildcard. The projection emits explicit verbs, and an
# action wildcard would silently confer every verb added later — the exact shape
# of "write conferred delete". A grant authorizes what it names.
action_matches(g) if input.action in g.actions

# `prefixes: []` ⇒ THE WHOLE BUCKET. Tested by shape: a grant whose `prefixes` is
# missing or not an array scopes NOTHING (this is where `not g.prefixes` would
# have been the C-3 trap in the other direction).
#
# `is_array` is load-bearing and was MISSING before review finding F3 — the same
# class of mistake, on the DATA side rather than the input side. `count` is
# polymorphic: `count("") == 0` and `count({}) == 0` are both true, so a grant
# carrying `"prefixes": ""` (or `{}`) classified as WHOLE BUCKET and authorized
# every key in it. Measured under opa 1.13.1 before the fix: a `read_objects`
# grant with `"prefixes": ""` allowed `anything/at/all`.
whole_bucket(g) if {
	is_array(g.prefixes)
	count(g.prefixes) == 0
}

applicable(g) if {
	bucket_matches(g)
	action_matches(g)
	conditions_hold(g)
}

# ── ABAC conditions (C-3) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# PRESENCE IS TESTED BY SHAPE, never by `not g.condition`, which is TRUE when the
# field is boolean `false` — i.e. it turns a malformed conditional grant into an
# unconditional allow. `is_array` also makes `conditions: []` (the unconditional
# case) explicit rather than incidental: `every` over an empty array holds
# vacuously, which is the intended meaning.

conditions_hold(g) if {
	is_array(g.conditions)
	every c in g.conditions {
		condition_matches(c)
	}
}

# Principal-attribute ABAC, membership semantics against the multi-valued
# attribute map the bundle publishes: email, email_domain, role, and one key per
# RLS namespace for users; client_id and role for service accounts. A condition
# naming a key the bundle does not carry is UNSATISFIABLE (the lookup is
# undefined), never vacuously true.
condition_matches(c) if {
	c.kind == "principal_attribute_equals"
	c.value in principal_attributes[c.key]
}

# Request-context ABAC. The key set is CLOSED and namespaced by the producer
# (`attributes["tag:tier"]`, not `attributes["tag"]`) — otherwise the client
# controls an arbitrary authorization namespace (§2.1).
condition_matches(c) if {
	c.kind == "request_attribute_equals"
	c.value in request_attributes[c.key]
}

# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Does some allow grant cover this request?
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

default grant_matches := false

# Object-shaped verbs: the key must fall under a granted prefix. A missing key on
# an object op matches NOTHING (it must not fall through to a keyless whole-bucket
# allow, which would bypass every prefix scope).
grant_matches if {
	input.action in object_actions
	is_string(input.object)
	some g in grants
	applicable(g)
	object_in_scope(g)
}

# Bucket-shaped verbs — today only `read` (HeadBucket, GetBucketLocation).
#
# DELIBERATELY NOT gated on `whole_bucket`, unlike every earlier version of this
# clause. That gate existed so a prefix-scoped grant could not confer a
# bucket-level POWER: deleting the bucket, rewriting its policy, scheduling a
# lifecycle rule. None of those verbs exist any more — bucket lifecycle and
# posture are control-plane. What is left is the disclosure that the bucket
# exists, and a principal scoped to `warehouse/team-a/*` demonstrably already
# knows that. Keeping the gate would make `HeadBucket` deny a bucket that
# `ListBuckets` had just listed to the same principal (see the header note).
grant_matches if {
	input.action in bucket_actions
	bucket_scoped
	some g in grants
	applicable(g)
}

# Listing: fail closed — see `list_scope_covers`.
grant_matches if {
	input.action in list_actions
	bucket_scoped
	some g in grants
	applicable(g)
	list_scope_covers(g)
}

# ListBuckets is account-scoped, so `bucket_matches` (which requires a non-empty
# bucket) cannot apply. A grant naming a concrete bucket makes THAT bucket
# visible; `"*"` makes the tenant's buckets visible. The response set is the
# `visible_buckets` / `all_buckets_visible` obligation.
grant_matches if {
	input.action in account_actions
	account_scoped
	some g in bucket_read_grants
}

# Every `read` grant that currently applies to this principal in this tenant,
# whatever bucket or prefix it names. Named for the verb, not for one op: it feeds
# ListBuckets authorization AND the visibility set. Deliberately not filtered by
# `whole_bucket` — a prefix-scoped `read` still discloses the bucket's name, which
# is all ListBuckets returns.
bucket_read_grants contains g if {
	some g in grants
	"read" in g.actions
	conditions_hold(g)
}

object_in_scope(g) if whole_bucket(g)

# Prefixes are literal S3 key prefixes. The projection appends a trailing "/" to
# every folder-scoped grant (`<h>/<b>/team-a` → `"team-a/"`, accepted defect D-4)
# so `startswith` cannot reach `team-a-private/`; this module must not
# re-introduce the hole by matching on unterminated prefixes.
#
# `is_array` is repeated here — `whole_bucket` already carries it — because
# `some p in <non-collection>` is NOT undefined in every engine. Measured on the
# same document, a grant carrying `"prefixes": ""`:
#
#   opa 1.13.1 -> undefined, so the decision is a clean
#                 `deny: no grant matches action and scope`
#   regorus    -> HARD EVALUATION ERROR, `some .. in collection expects
#                 array/set/object. Got ""`, and the entrypoint returns no
#                 decision at all
#
# regorus is the engine the gateway runs, so without this the module's stated
# "a grant whose `prefixes` is not an array scopes NOTHING" is delivered only by
# the test oracle and not in production — and an *erroring* PDP is a decision
# the PEP has to invent, which is the shape of a fail-open. Rule 1 again: shape
# is tested explicitly, never inferred from an engine's undefined-value
# semantics. Same guard on all three `prefixes` iteration sites.
object_in_scope(g) if {
	is_array(g.prefixes)
	some p in g.prefixes
	startswith(input.object, p)
}

# LISTS FAIL CLOSED. The requested prefix must lie WITHIN a granted prefix. In
# particular an UNBOUNDED list (`requested_prefix == ""`) is covered only by a
# whole-bucket grant, because every emitted prefix ends in "/" and is therefore
# non-empty. The alternative — silently rewriting an unbounded list down to the
# granted prefixes — puts the PEP in charge of enforcement and fails open the
# moment an obligation is dropped.
list_scope_covers(g) if whole_bucket(g)

list_scope_covers(g) if {
	is_array(g.prefixes)
	some p in g.prefixes
	startswith(requested_prefix, p)
}

default requested_prefix := ""

requested_prefix := p if {
	p := input.prefix
	is_string(p)
}

# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Deny — overrides allow, unconditionally
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# A malformed `prefixes` means the OPPOSITE thing on the two sides, and it has
# to. On the allow side (`whole_bucket`) it scopes NOTHING; reading it as the
# whole bucket would be an over-grant. On the deny side it must cover the WHOLE
# BUCKET; reading it as "scopes nothing" would turn a corrupt revocation into a
# silent fail-open. Same shape test, opposite safe default — this is rule 4's
# "opposite empty-case semantics" applied to the malformed case.
deny_in_scope(g) if object_in_scope(g)

deny_in_scope(g) if not is_array(g.prefixes)

deny_covers_listing(g) if list_scope_covers(g)

deny_covers_listing(g) if not is_array(g.prefixes)

default explicit_deny := false

explicit_deny if {
	input.action in object_actions
	some g in deny_grants
	applicable(g)
	deny_in_scope(g)
}

# SCOPE asymmetry, for every bucket-shaped verb. A bucket-level op has no prefix
# dimension, so a PREFIX-scoped deny of that verb blocks it outright instead of
# being ignored — the conservative reading, since there is no way to honour the
# prefix on a request that names no key. `applicable(g)` action-matches, so the
# deny still only revokes the verbs it names.
#
# Review finding F4 also required a VERB asymmetry here — a second clause under
# which ANY deny in the bucket, whatever verb it named, blocked
# `prefix_defeating_bucket_actions` = {`delete_bucket`, `write_bucket_config`},
# because those two defeat a prefix-scoped deny without naming it (one destroys
# the denied keys, the other rewrites the policy protecting them). That clause is
# REMOVED with those verbs (2026-08-08): bucket lifecycle and posture are
# control-plane now, and F4 itself argued the rule must NOT extend to `read_bucket`
# — "blocking it on an unrelated deny buys no security and breaks HeadBucket for
# anyone who happens to carry one deny anywhere in the bucket". `read` is that
# verb. So the removal is what F4 asked for, not a relaxation of it.
explicit_deny if {
	input.action in bucket_actions
	bucket_scoped
	some g in deny_grants
	applicable(g)
}

explicit_deny if {
	input.action in list_actions
	bucket_scoped
	some g in deny_grants
	applicable(g)
	deny_covers_listing(g)
}

# ListBuckets: a whole-tenant deny on `read` blocks the call outright. A deny
# naming one bucket only removes that bucket — handled in `visible_buckets`.
#
# `account_scoped` is load-bearing now that `read` is in BOTH `bucket_actions` and
# `account_actions`: without it this clause would also fire on a HeadBucket, where
# the bucket-shaped clause above is the one that must decide.
explicit_deny if {
	input.action in account_actions
	account_scoped
	some g in deny_grants
	"read" in g.actions
	g.bucket == "*"
	whole_bucket(g)
	conditions_hold(g)
}

# ── the list-key-name leak guard (accepted defect C-1) ──────────────────────
#
# THIS SET IS DELIBERATELY NOT ACTION-MATCHED. A listing returns key NAMES, so a
# deny that makes those keys unreadable must still remove them from the listing:
# the motivating case is a deny on `read_objects` while `list_objects` is granted.
# Requiring the deny grant's `actions` to contain `list_objects` (which is what
# `applicable_grant` did) leaves the leak wide open.
#
# Conditions ARE evaluated — a deny that does not currently apply to this
# principal is not a deny — and the bucket must match, or one bucket's deny would
# censor another's listing.

listing_denies contains g if {
	some g in deny_grants
	bucket_matches(g)
	conditions_hold(g)
}

default list_leak_deny := false

# The whole requested listing scope sits inside the deny: there is nothing left
# to return, so deny the call rather than allow an empty listing (an empty 200
# and a 403 are different facts, and the audit trail should record the 403).
list_leak_deny if {
	input.action in list_actions
	some g in listing_denies
	deny_covers_listing(g)
}

# Deny prefixes that fall INSIDE the requested listing scope. The PEP must drop
# those keys from the response — hence `must_understand`.
excluded_prefix_set contains p if {
	some g in listing_denies
	is_array(g.prefixes)
	some p in g.prefixes
	startswith(p, requested_prefix)
}

excluded_prefixes := sort([p | some p in excluded_prefix_set])

# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# ListBuckets visibility
#
# `visible_buckets: []` means NOTHING VISIBLE — the OPPOSITE of `prefixes: []`.
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# B-2 / C-8: `all_buckets_visible` is the ONLY unfiltered path, so it may not be
# emitted when ANY deny grant or ANY denylist entry exists for this principal in
# this tenant — the enumerated form is used instead, which subtracts them.
default all_buckets_visible := false

all_buckets_visible if {
	input.action in account_actions
	account_scoped
	some g in bucket_read_grants
	g.bucket == "*"
	whole_bucket(g)
	count(deny_grants) == 0
	count(denylisted_buckets) == 0
}

# Buckets whose CRD denylist names this principal (RAW sub, §1.7).
denylisted_buckets contains b if {
	buckets := data.tenants[input.tenant].bucket_attributes
	is_object(buckets)
	some b, attrs in buckets
	is_object(attrs.denylist)
	some denied_sub, _ in attrs.denylist
	denied_sub == input.principal.sub
}

# INCLUSIVE of prefix-scoped grants: no `whole_bucket(g)` here, deliberately. See
# the header note — ListBuckets returns only the NAME, and a principal scoped to
# `warehouse/team-a/*` must already know `warehouse` to use its own grant.
visible_bucket_set contains b if {
	some g in bucket_read_grants
	g.bucket != "*"
	b := g.bucket
	not bucket_hidden(b)
}

# A `"*"` grant is enumerated against the tenant's known buckets rather than
# passed through, so the deny subtraction below can apply. Buckets with no
# HFBucket CR are not enumerated — an under-listing, which is the safe direction,
# and since 2026-08-08 the gateway can no longer CREATE such a bucket, so the set
# of CR-less buckets can only shrink.
visible_bucket_set contains b if {
	some g in bucket_read_grants
	g.bucket == "*"
	buckets := data.tenants[input.tenant].bucket_attributes
	is_object(buckets)
	some b, _ in buckets
	not bucket_hidden(b)
}

visible_buckets := sort([b | some b in visible_bucket_set])

bucket_hidden(b) if b in denylisted_buckets

bucket_hidden(b) if {
	some g in deny_grants
	"read" in g.actions
	conditions_hold(g)
	deny_covers_bucket(g, b)
}

deny_covers_bucket(g, b) if g.bucket == b

deny_covers_bucket(g, _) if g.bucket == "*"

# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Obligations
#
# At most one body can hold at a time, so this stays a well-formed complete rule.
# `list_actions` is disjoint from the other two, and the two account bodies are
# split by a boolean.
#
# The `account_scoped` gate on the last two is NOT decoration. `read` is in both
# `bucket_actions` and `account_actions`, so without it a permitted HeadBucket
# would carry a `visible_buckets` / `all_buckets_visible` obligation — an
# obligation about a ListBuckets response, attached to a response that has no
# bucket list in it. `must_understand` makes that fatal by design: a PEP that
# cannot apply a named obligation must deny, so HeadBucket would break for
# everyone. Shape gates the rule, exactly as module rule 3 requires.
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

default obligations := {}

obligations := {
	"excluded_prefixes": excluded_prefixes,
	"must_understand": ["excluded_prefixes"],
} if {
	input.action in list_actions
	count(excluded_prefixes) > 0
}

obligations := {"all_buckets_visible": true} if {
	input.action in account_actions
	account_scoped
	all_buckets_visible
}

obligations := {
	"visible_buckets": visible_buckets,
	"must_understand": ["visible_buckets"],
} if {
	input.action in account_actions
	account_scoped
	not all_buckets_visible
}
